title: Working in the houserules kit repository

entries.summary: Edit the kit in `template/`, then run `houserules update --dir .`; never hand-edit the root copies or the generated rules and skill.
body: This repository runs its own kit. The root copies of every `KIT_OWNED` path — `tools/`, `.claude/agents/`, and the kit skills — are the installed copy; `template/` is the source that `init` and `update` ship to every project.

`crates/houserules/tests/dogfood.rs` pins every root copy to its template source byte for byte (ported from `tests/dogfood.test.mjs`, retired at batch 20 T3, HR-047); a hand edit fails the test and is lost on the next update. `update` runs through the compiled `houserules` binary (batch 18 T6, docs/specs/2026-09-05-batch-18-phase3.md §4); `bin/houserules.mjs` retired outright at batch 20 T3 along with the rest of the JS toolchain (`houserules.payload-runs-on-builtins`).
`.claude/rules/*.md` and `.claude/skills/project-knowledge/SKILL.md` are generated by `houserules render` from `knowledge/`.

entries.summary: Treat the tag-pilot checkout outside this repository as read-only: never modify it, commit there, run its agents, or run `init` or `update` against it.
body: tag-pilot (branch `knowledge-management`, PR #42) is the origin of this kit and, until the adoption ruling in docs/design.md §5.4, the upstream of every kit-owned file.
Before every release, diff its `tools/`, `.claude/agents/`, and `.claude/skills/` against `template/` and port the drift; the first port is `process.evals-rerun` with its `co-change` check (HR-003).

entries.summary: Live-run every CLI change in a scratch `git init` repo: `init --dir <scratch>`, both checks inside; each gate its own `live_run` entry with `exit`.
body: Scratch repositories live under the session scratchpad, never inside this repository and never in tag-pilot. Run `houserules check-knowledge` and `houserules check-backlog` there and record each command's verbatim output as its own report `live_run` entry (batch 3 task 3 recorded only one of a chained pair).

Batch 18 T6 flips the binary this recipe runs (docs/specs/2026-09-05-batch-18-phase3.md §4): until HR-048 ships a distribution channel, exercise the compiled binary directly — `cargo build --release` once, then `target/release/houserules <command>` (or `cargo run --quiet --release --bin houserules -- <command>`) against the scratch repository. The npm-era HR-001 pair (`pnpm dlx`'s published path, the symlinked `node_modules` path) no longer applies, and neither does the frozen file itself: `bin/houserules.mjs` retired outright at batch 20 T3 (HR-047, docs/specs/2026-09-07-batch-20-phase5.md §2) along with the rest of the JS toolchain — it only ever implemented `init`/`update`/`files`, and this recipe's compiled-binary form already covered the same surface.
For a change to `update`, run `init` and then `update` in the same scratch repository and confirm that only kit-owned files changed.
The report names the scratch path (a `cd` entry or the path in the command) and records the init and both check gates as their own `live_run` entries; a live run without them fails the recipe.

A fix round that changes no CLI behavior (test-only, report-only, evidence wording) may stand on the task's original live run when the report discloses the scoping for the re-reviewer to judge (batch 6).

Sandboxing a real cargo-dist shell installer (batch 27 T2, HR-133) inside a scratch `HOME` needs `CARGO_HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` unset too, not only `HOME` overridden: the installer's own install-path fallback and axoupdater's receipt-home lookup both prefer `CARGO_HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` first when either is inherited from the real environment, silently installing into the real machine's `~/.cargo/bin` even with a scratch `HOME` set (`env -u CARGO_HOME -u XDG_CONFIG_HOME HOME=<scratch> sh`). Caught live when this exact mistake overwrote this repository's own dev-installed `houserules` binary; fixed by reinstalling from the tree (`cargo install --path crates/houserules --bin houserules --force`).

entries.summary: Relative to tag-pilot: unprefixed agent and skill names, `project-knowledge` skill, `dependency_vetting` for field `a19`, parameterized id prefix.
body: Agents: `tagpilot-implementer` → `implementer`, `tagpilot-task-reviewer` → `task-reviewer`, `tagpilot-branch-reviewer` → `branch-reviewer`. Skills: `tagpilot-orchestrating` → `orchestrating`, `tagpilot-knowledge` → `project-knowledge`.
Backlog ids: `TP-` → `--id-prefix` (default `WI`, `HR` in this repository). The install stamp is `.houserules.json`.
The kit was named lorekit until 2026-08-31; docs/design.md §5.1 records the rename.

entries.summary: The vendored payload runs on the `houserules` binary and POSIX shell only: every shipped reference invokes it directly; no file needs Node, npm, or an install.
body: Amended at batch 18 T6 (docs/specs/2026-09-05-batch-18-phase3.md §1, parent spec docs/specs/2026-09-04-batch-15-tier2-spec.md §2, RULED at the Tier-2 spec's approval, 2026-09-04): the prior invariant ("Node built-ins and POSIX shell only") held while the payload's own engines were `.mjs` files; it stops being true the moment a shipped reference stops being runnable by `node` alone. The id is unchanged (`knowledge-base.ids-are-permanent`); only the body restates the now-true contract.
The SessionStart hook and the CI gates run where nothing but the `houserules` binary and a POSIX shell are guaranteed; a runtime dependency would break both (docs/design.md §2–3).

`tools/kb.sh` and `tools/backlog.sh` left the payload (batch 18 T5, docs/specs/2026-09-05-batch-18-phase3.md §§1,3): every shipped reference to them rewrote to the flat `houserules` command, and `update` deletes either file an install still carries.

A template script may exec an optional tool only behind a probe of that tool itself, with a working fallback; probing mise is not probing the tool (batch 6 task 4). The shipped `.githooks/commit-msg` execs `houserules check-commit` only behind a probe of that subcommand; when the probe fails, nothing runs and the commit is not blocked (design.md 5.81(2) dropped the shipped hook's own trailer gate — attribution enforcement is fully project-ruled now: a project's own attribution gate comes from its own `commits`-type entry, which `check-commit` picks up the same way it picks up `process.conventional-commits`). This repository's own devDependencies (vitest) serve its own tests only and never enter `template/`.

The seeded CI gate (`template/.github/workflows/knowledge.yml`) now carries an install step (batch 19 T2, HR-063): the cargo-dist shell installer on the releases/latest alias fetches the `houserules` binary from `jblossey/houserules`'s own GitHub Releases before `check-knowledge`/`check-backlog`/`audit` run, under `shell: bash` (fix round 1) so a failed download aborts the step instead of the pipe's `sh` masking curl's exit code (GitHub's own documented default, `bash -e {0}` with no `-o pipefail`, only applies `-o pipefail` when `shell: bash` is named). The wiring exists; a release with real assets does not yet (HR-048's pipeline has cut one release, zero assets), so a fresh `houserules init` today seeds a PR gate whose install step genuinely fails red, on curl's own 404, until the pipeline cuts a release with assets (docs/specs/2026-09-06-batch-19-phase4.md §7's step two) — this invariant is amended against that known gap, not silently past it.

The second known gap (batch 18 branch review) closed at batch 20 T2 (HR-066, docs/specs/2026-09-07-batch-20-phase5.md §3): `check-report-claims` now ships as the `houserules check-report-claims` subcommand (`crates/houserules/src/report_claims.rs`, moved from a dev-only `src/bin/` target), so the seeded implementer template's closing act invokes the binary the payload itself carries, in every adopter repo.

source.ref: parent spec docs/specs/2026-09-04-batch-15-tier2-spec.md §2 (owner ruling at approval); docs/design.md §2–3

entries.summary: Use cargo for every package operation in this repository (`cargo add <crate>@=<version>`); pnpm, npm, and npx left the toolchain at batch 20 T3.
body: Amended at batch 20 T3 (HR-047, docs/specs/2026-09-07-batch-20-phase5.md §2): the prior rule (owner ruling of 2026-09-01, pnpm for every JS package operation) held while this repository still carried a JS dev-tooling layer (vitest, package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml); it stops being true the moment that layer retires. The id is unchanged (`knowledge-base.ids-are-permanent`); only the body restates the now-true contract, the same pattern `houserules.payload-runs-on-builtins`'s own doc already used for an equivalent ending.

The workspace is now Rust-only: `rust` is `mise.toml`'s one pinned tool, `Cargo.lock` is the only lockfile, and the mise tasks are `setup`, `test`, `houserules`, `lint`, and `audit` — `setup` no longer runs a package-manager install step (there is no package manager left to run one with).
The payload in `template/` still has no dependency and no install step (`houserules.payload-runs-on-builtins`); this ruling changes nothing there, same as before.

entries.summary: When `KIT_OWNED` gains or loses a path, update README's agent-layer bullet and ownership table in the same commit.
body: README.md enumerates the kit-owned skills twice: the agent-layer bullet and the ownership-manifest table.
No test pins these enumerations; batch 5's task 1 review caught both stale after KIT_OWNED grew. A co-change check would misfire (bin changes without README constantly), so the rule stays judged.

entries.summary: release-please's config JSON schema omits prerelease-type and skip-snapshot from its root; keep those settings under the package entry.
body: The schema at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/release-please/v17.11.2/schemas/config.json sets `additionalProperties: false` on the config root. The root's own `properties` list omits `prerelease-type` and `skip-snapshot`. `src/manifest.ts` reads both at the top level, like `versioning` and `release-type`. The project's docs show a top-level example with `prerelease-type`. The omission is a gap in the schema, not the runtime.

Verified with `ajv-cli validate`. A root-level `prerelease-type` key fails with `params.additionalProperty: 'prerelease-type'` (`must NOT have additional properties`). The identical key nested under a `packages` entry validates cleanly: that path's value schema (`ReleaserConfigOptions`, reached through `allOf`) carries no such restriction.

Put `prerelease-type`, `skip-snapshot`, and the other release settings under the package's own entry in `release-please-config.json` (`packages['crates/houserules']` as of HR-073, batch 20 T5; `packages['.']` before it), not at the config root. `src/manifest.ts` merges each package's config over the root default per key, so a single-package repository behaves identically either way. Only the nested placement passes the schema the file's own `$schema` points at.

entries.summary: Every test that mints a scratch directory registers its removal at the mkdtemp site: `tempfile::TempDir`'s own Drop, or an equivalent Drop-owning guard.
body: At the batch 9 task 2 review, tests/ held 21 mkdtempSync call sites across seven vitest files with no cleanup; a full suite run left /tmp holding 1714 orphaned houserules-target-* trees plus 89 kb-* and 15 ws-* trees, and a transient inode exhaustion had already broken one suite attempt.

Batch 20 T3 (HR-047, docs/specs/2026-09-07-batch-20-phase5.md §2) retired the vitest suite entirely, along with its own shared helper (tests/scratch-dir.mjs's scratchDir(prefix), registering rmSync on onTestFinished) and the JS-only sanctioned forms this rule used to enumerate. Cargo's own tests are the only suite left, and `tempfile` (this crate's `[dev-dependencies]`) already gives every ordinary scratch directory the guarantee this rule exists to require: `tempfile::tempdir()` returns a `TempDir` whose `Drop` removes it, with no registration step of its own to forget.

The one sanctioned form beyond a bare `TempDir`: a Drop-owning guard for anything `tempfile` cannot mint directly, the same shape `tests/common/mod.rs`'s `FrozenWorktree` already uses for a detached git worktree (a `git worktree add` at a fresh temp path, `git worktree remove --force` in its own `Drop`, with the removal path assigned before any fallible step runs so a panicking test still cleans up during unwind). `gen-goldens.rs`'s own `ScratchDir` is the one case with no test-runner cleanup expectation at all (a `src/bin/*.rs` target, not a test; Cargo does not link `[dev-dependencies]` into a binary target, so `tempfile` is unavailable there) -- it still keeps a Drop guard of its own, over `std::env::temp_dir()` directly, for the same reason every scratch directory keeps one.

source.ref: batch 9 task 2 review; batch 9 branch review rider; HR-035

entries.summary: After a release-please PR merge, check for baseline drift with update --dir .; the version already rides the PR. See docs/runbook.md.
body: release-please bumps crates/houserules/Cargo.toml's version in its PR (the release-type: rust config's own native update, HR-073, batch 20 T5, closing the gap package.json's batch 20 T3 (HR-047) retirement had opened) and, in the SAME PR, rewrites .houserules.json's version field to match, via an extra-files json/jsonpath entry (/.houserules.json, $.version -- branch review batch 24, issue 2: folding the restamp into the release PR is what makes the mechanism testable before merge, not only on main after it). Merging the PR therefore leaves the version stamp already correct: crates/houserules/tests/dogfood.rs's houserules_json_stamps_the_installed_version_and_the_hr_id_prefix test (HR-044, which pins the stamp to CARGO_PKG_VERSION) passes on the release PR itself, before merge, by construction.

What the PR does not update is baselines: the per-file hashes houserules update --dir . stamps for every KIT_OWNED file and kit-shipped knowledge entry, which can still drift if the kit's own payload changed since the last stamp -- independent of the version bump. After you merge a release-please PR: run `houserules update --dir .` (it prints the drift line, for example `kit 0.3.0 -> 0.3.0` when the version already matches); commit `.houserules.json` only if a baseline hash changed, as `chore(release): restamp the kit baselines`; push to main.
Full steps and rationale: docs/runbook.md.

In a project that installs the kit: install the newer `houserules` binary first (whichever channel the project used -- the shell installer, mise, or a direct download; otherwise the command below still runs the old binary and reads no drift), then run `houserules update --dir .` the same way the kit repository itself does, and commit `.houserules.json` only when the drift line's sides differ. The finishing-a-feature skill ships this unified form (batch 19 T2 fix round 1: npm retirement removed the earlier pnpm-exec-only path this bullet used to describe).

entries.summary: tests/fixtures/batch14-workspace/ commits gitignored .superpowers/ batch-14 deliverables verbatim, host paths neutralized.
body: .gitignore excludes .superpowers/, so CI never checks it out; the validate/stats/audit parity tests need the twelve batch-14 deliverables' real content, not scalar values, so they are committed copies under tests/fixtures/, not live reads of the gitignored workspace.
The batch 16 task 1 review checked all twelve files for public-tree fitness: no credential, token, API key, email address, session URL, or third-party data.

Their embedded absolute host paths were neutralized to a /home/maintainer/... prefix on 2026-09-11 (owner ruling, public-surface sweep, HR-093); the fixture otherwise freezes its inputs unchanged, and crates/houserules/tests/validate_stats_audit_parity.rs asserts the neutralized prefix.

Relocated from tests/corpus/fixtures/ at batch 20 T3 (HR-047, docs/specs/2026-09-07-batch-20-phase5.md §2): tests/corpus/ (the frozen JS-parity captures and manifest) retired with the rest of the vitest layer, but this directory is input data, not JS parity output, so it moved rather than re-baselined -- crates/houserules/tests/validate_stats_audit_parity.rs remains its largest reader.

entries.summary: A committed test or fixture that pins a git sha must pin one on main's ancestry, proven reachable in a fresh clone.
body: This repository merges fast-forward from aggregated commits, so pre-aggregation branch shas are discarded and become unreachable from every ref; a workspace archive's base/head values name exactly such shas (batch 16 task 1, finding 1: four of them, resolvable locally, unresolvable in any fresh clone).
Prove reachability the way the fix did: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main` inside a `git clone --no-local` of the repository, and run the RED/GREEN of the pinning test in that clone.
A CI job that checks out a pinned sha as a worktree needs `fetch-depth: 0` on its checkout (batch 16: T2 removed it as unused, T3 had to restore it for the frozen-worktree parity tests).

source.ref: batch 16 task 1 review finding 1; branch review retrospective

entries.summary: A tag or commit pushed with the default GITHUB_TOKEN triggers no workflow; a release hand-off needs a PAT/App token or an explicit workflow_dispatch hop.
body: GitHub suppresses workflow runs for events created with the default GITHUB_TOKEN to prevent recursion; workflow_dispatch and repository_dispatch are the documented exceptions that always create runs (batch 16 T5 review finding 1, verified against live docs in the fix round).

Consequence for the Tier-2 phase-4 wiring: release-please tagging with the default token will never start a tag-triggered dist workflow. Options recorded in the T5 doc: a PAT or GitHub App token on the tagging step, or a workflow_dispatch call gated on release_created output. The choice is an open phase-4 question for the owner.

source.ref: batch 16 task 5 review finding 1; t5-cross-compilation.md trigger section

entries.summary: Bump rust with `V=$(mise latest rust) && mise use --pin rust@$V` — stable's newest, resolved by the CLI, exact in mise.toml; keep the components table.
body: Owner ruling at the batch 16 report (docs/design.md §5.27): the repo standardizes on stable-freshest for toolchain bumps, deliberately bypassing mise's minimum_release_age quarantine for the rust toolchain; the exact-pins rule still holds — the number in mise.toml comes from the CLI, never from memory.

Gotcha found applying the ruling: when mise.toml already holds a table entry, `mise use --pin rust@stable` writes the literal keyword `stable` instead of a resolved version. Resolve first (`mise latest rust`), then pin the resolved value; confirm `components = ["clippy", "rustfmt"]` survived — CI's fmt and clippy steps need them on fresh runners.
After a bump, run the cargo gates (fmt --check, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test) before committing mise.toml.

entries.summary: Where the frozen JS crashed or a glob/regex fails to compile, the binary reports one named error or finding — never a reproduced crash, never a silent default.
body: Spec §6's crash-path and CLI-failure-path rulings, extracted so they load with the files they govern. The two failure shapes to refuse: a panic/.expect on data an adopter can write (reproduces the crash), and an unwrap_or(default) on a Result whose error the ruling says must be named (swallows it — batch 17 T3 fix round 1 issue 4, and the report-field workspace residual the batch 17 branch review found at audit.rs:558).

Absence stays tolerated exactly as the JS tolerates it; the named-error contract covers present-but-malformed data and compile failures. One stderr line naming the data, exit 2 for load/usage arms; a named finding row where the surface reports findings.

In a parity port, name an error arm only where the reference engine itself errors — measure the reference first (batch 18 T3: merge_settings named two arms the frozen JS seeds cleanly, because the JS's ??= replaces null; the fix re-measured both engines and mirrored).

Two recurring shapes count as reproduced crashes (batch 22 T1/T2, each filed twice before landing): a synthesized io::Error replacing the operating system's own error text, and a silent skip of an unreadable directory entry. Report the OS's error verbatim; only NotFound is tolerable absence.

entries.summary: Dev tooling is a cargo bin under crates/houserules/src/bin/; never a new Node script.
body: Owner ruling at the batch 17 report, applied at batch 18 T5 fix round 1 when find-shell-tool-refs.mjs and diff-shape-gate.mjs were ported to cargo bins in the same round that added them.
tools/make-corpus.mjs was the one ruled interim exception (docs/design.md decision 30); it retired with the frozen JS at Tier-2 phase 5 (batch 20 T3, HR-047).
The ruling previously had no loading path for tools/**; this entry gives it one so a dispatch touching tools/ carries it without --ids.

diff-shape-gate.rs itself completed and retired at batch 21 (HR-093): it proved the batch 18 T5 corpus-to-goldens re-shape changed only the flat-command rewrite, category by category, and held through the last commit where the proof held -- batch 21 T2 fix round 1's second commit. Batch 21 T2 fix round 1's PROTOCOL edit (the very next commit in that round) legitimately edited a generated file's source and regenerated it in the same commit, which expired the proof permanently -- the gate's new side read the working tree while its old side was pinned to frozen git history, so no later regeneration could ever bring them back into agreement. Retired rather than re-pinned: a gate with both sides frozen to immutable refs compares two constants forever, which proves nothing further. After the deletion, find-shell-tool-refs.rs is the only bin under this rule that uses walkdir; gen-goldens.rs still carries its own recursive copy_dir_recursive (fs::read_dir plus recursion, no walkdir). (Branch review, important issue 2: the original two SHAs cited here, 2f3e633 and 218e0a8, predate batch 21's mid-batch rebase and are reachable from no branch; named by batch/task/round/subject instead, since that locator survives every future re-SHA that a rebase or aggregation performs.)

source.ref: owner ruling, batch 17 report; batch 18 task-5-review.json important finding; docs/design.md decision 30

entries.summary: release.yml is generated from dist-workspace.toml; never hand-edit it — edit the config and run `dist generate` (`dist generate --check` is the gate).
body: cargo-dist's `dist generate` rewrites the whole file from `dist-workspace.toml` on every run; a hand-edit is silently discarded the next time anyone runs `dist init`, `dist generate`, or `dist update`, and `dist generate --check` fails once a hand-edit diverges from what the config would produce.

Landed at batch 19 T1 with the config's own header comment stating the same discipline; this entry gives the generated file's own path a loading path so an agent about to edit release.yml directly sees the rule, per knowledge-base.rules-need-a-loading-path (batch 19 T1 fix round 1, review issue 4).

An installer-only setting such as `install-path` leaves `release.yml` byte-identical after `dist generate`: the value bakes into the generated installer script at release-build time, not into the CI workflow file. `dist generate --check` exiting 0 with an empty diff is exactly this outcome, not a sign the edit went unread (batch 27 T1, HR-135's install-path move, live-verified with `dist build --artifacts=global`).

entries.summary: An Actions run step with no shell key runs bash -e without pipefail: a failing left side of a pipe passes silently; name shell: bash for -eo pipefail.
body: GitHub's own workflow-syntax doc (jobs.<job_id>.steps[*].shell) documents the asymmetry: the unspecified default and the explicit shell: bash differ exactly by -o pipefail (and --noprofile --norc).

Batch 19 T2: the seeded curl|sh install step returned green on a live 404 until shell: bash was named; reproduced both ways and as an Actions-resolved run at exit 22 (t2-evidence/pipeline-no-pipefail.log, pipeline-with-pipefail.log, seeded-install-step-live-r3-paste.log). Applies to every piped run step, this repository's workflows and the seeded template's alike.

entries.summary: A test that pins a path the binary prints builds it component by component: Path::join keeps an embedded slash, and Windows alone shows the divergence.
body: rustc 1.98.1's library/std/src/path.rs (PathBuf::_push) appends a relative path verbatim after one MAIN_SEPARATOR_STR. It re-joins components with that separator only behind a verbatim (\\?\) prefix. So on Windows dir.join("knowledge/process.json") displays as ...\knowledge/process.json, while rules::model::load_base's own root.join("knowledge") then dir.join(name) displays as ...\knowledge\process.json.

Batch 20 T6 fix round 2 (HR-085): that one character was the whole windows-latest failure of crates/houserules/tests/install.rs's init_reports_a_render_failure_on_broken_project_data_as_one_usage_error (run 34220012072, job 102040656623). Linux and macOS never show it, because / is their own separator. tempfile paths are the exposed case; repo_root() canonicalizes, and the verbatim prefix that produces normalizes the join away.

Two controls in that same file pin the correct shape, and both passed in that same Windows run. Each compares a printed path against the binary's own stderr. The marker pin is init_reports_an_unparsable_pre_existing_marker_as_a_named_error_exit_2: a one-component dir.path().join(".houserules.json"), which proves the tempdir prefix round-trips exactly. The settings pin is init_reports_a_scalar_hooks_value_as_a_named_error_exit_2 and init_reports_a_scalar_session_start_value_as_a_named_error_exit_2: they assert_eq! stderr against format!("{}: ...", settings_path.display()), where the test's dir.path().join(".claude/settings.json") and the binary's target.join(SETTINGS_PATH) build the path from the identical string, which proves an identical-string join interoperates. Mirror the construction the code uses. Never loosen the assertion to a substring instead.

A gate finding printed with an absolute path is itself the violation shape (batch 22 T1 round 2): findings pin repository-relative paths built as strings, and the test builds its expectation the same way the code builds the message.

entries.summary: Pin every workflow `uses:` to a full commit SHA, version tag as a comment; the Actions policy rejects a tag ref; release.yml pins live in dist-workspace.toml.
body: The repository setting `sha_pinning_required` (Settings > Actions > General) fails any workflow run that references an action by tag or branch, and the allowed-actions policy is `selected`: GitHub-owned, verified creators, and the explicit patterns jdx/mise-action, googleapis/release-please-action, swatinem/rust-cache. A new action needs its pattern added there before its first run.

Resolve a pin with the CLI, never from memory: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<tag> --jq .sha`, then the precise tag for the comment from `repos/<owner>/<repo>/tags`. Dependabot (github-actions ecosystem) moves the SHA and the comment together on its weekly run.

release.yml is generated (dist-workspace.toml is the source): add or bump a pin in `[dist.github-action-commits]` and run `dist generate`; `dist` picks the action version itself, so after a `cargo-dist-version` bump grep the regenerated file for any `uses:` without a 40-hex ref and pin it there.

entries.summary: Gate platform-specific code with #[cfg]: a std::os::unix or std::os::windows use compiles only on that platform; CI builds all targets on three OSes.
body: Batch 21 T1 fix rounds 3-4 added three tests using std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt ungated; cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --all-targets failed E0433 in both affected test targets, so windows-latest clippy and test could not compile. The defect survived five review rounds and two controller gate sweeps because every proof ran on Linux.

The crate's own precedent is the gate: install.rs, commit_msg_hook.rs, and validate_stats_audit_parity.rs all cfg-gate their os::unix uses, with a #[cfg(windows)] arm where the behavior needs a Windows equivalent.

The cheap local proxy runs in mise run lint since batch 21: cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --all-targets --locked, with the target provisioned by mise.toml's rust targets option. The host's green cargo test proves one OS of three.

Second layer, found on PR #14's real macos-latest run after #[cfg(unix)] shipped (the same three tests then panicked at an fs::write unwrap, Os error 92 Illegal byte sequence, since APFS rejects a non-UTF-8 filename at creation): a cfg gate names one CAPABILITY at a time, so #[cfg(unix)] covering the compiler capability (OsStrExt exists) does not cover a distinct filesystem capability (writing that name succeeds) the same test also needs and Linux alone has both of; the fix (seed via git's byte-oriented index -- git hash-object -w --stdin, git update-index --add --cacheinfo -- never a real file write) is recorded at its call site, `crates/houserules/src/rules/check.rs`'s `seed_undecodable_tracked_path`.

entries.summary: A task-end gate run includes every check CI runs on push or pull request; a local gate list that omits a CI check is stale.
body: The list today: a mingw-w64 C compiler installed first (`gcc-mingw-w64-x86-64`, needed once a `-sys` crate landed, houserules.c-toolchain-crates-need-ci-mingw), cargo fmt --check, the full suite, clippy, the cross-target check, the lint chain (shellcheck, cargo deny, both knowledge gates, render --check, the residue gate, the vacuous-exception gate, the payload-stamp gate, the dist-generate-check gate), and -- pull-request only -- a check-commit range pass (`houserules check-commit --from $(git merge-base main HEAD) --to HEAD`, ci.yml's own check-commit job) and a knowledge-base audit of the diff (`mise run audit -- --base <PR base> --head <PR head>`).
Derive the list from .github/workflows and mise.toml, not from memory; when CI gains a check, the task-end list gains it in the same change.

The check-commit range pass matters most for a per-commit knowledge check: it judges every commit back to the real merge base with main, never only a fix round's own diff, so an omission here is exactly how a per-commit check ships unrun against the range CI actually judges (batch 24 T1 fix round 6: a per-commit co-change check went unrun at CI's own --from until this entry named the job).
Origin: batch 22 T1 - three review rounds closed with cargo fmt --check red at HEAD because no round's gate list named it; CI would have failed the first push.

entries.summary: The embedded payload carries the build checkout's exact bytes; template/ stays `-text` so every build host embeds LF and seeded gates stay green.
body: `install.rs`'s `Payload` (`rust-embed`) walks `template/` at compile time and bakes each file's bytes into the binary as that checkout holds them. Git's line-ending conversion runs per checkout: Windows defaults `core.autocrlf` to `true`, so a Windows-built binary embeds `template/**`'s text files with CRLF unless `.gitattributes` marks that tree `-text`. `init` and `update` write the embedded bytes straight into the seeded install, and `check-backlog`'s emitter round-trip gate compares them against the shipped emitter's own LF output, so a CRLF seed fails that gate on every install a Windows-built binary produces -- a product defect, not a test artifact.

First surfaced in batch 22's first three-OS CI run: two archive.rs tests that init-seed a scratch repo and expect check-backlog green failed on the windows-latest leg, with backlog/schema.json and every backlog file the round-trip gate compares reported as diverging.

dogfood.rs's parity tests (root_kit_owned_files_equal_their_template_source_byte_for_byte and its neighbors) compare the root copies against `template/` byte for byte, so a `-text` scope limited to `template/` still fails them on a Windows checkout once `template/` alone is fixed and the root copies still convert to CRLF: byte-stability has to be repository-wide (`* -text` at the top of `.gitattributes`), not template-only.

entries.summary: Touching template/ also needs crates/houserules/payload.stamp regenerated: `cargo run --bin payload-stamp-gate -- --write`, or mise run lint fails.
body: HR-081: release-please's commit-to-package attribution (CommitSplit, keyed on a commit's changed file paths) only ever counts a commit that touches crates/houserules/**, and include-component-in-tag stays false (design.md 5.20, reaffirmed at 5.72 after a since-rejected reversal at 5.71), which rules out linking a second package's commits in via any component-matching plugin (getComponent always returns '' when that setting is false). A template/**-only commit would otherwise cut no release, even though template/ is embedded into the shipped binary at compile time (houserules.payload-embeds-checkout-bytes) and is therefore a real product change.

crates/houserules/payload.stamp records a sha256 digest of template/'s current tracked file set (paths and content). payload-stamp-gate (crates/houserules/src/bin/payload-stamp-gate.rs, wired into `mise run lint` alongside residue-gate) recomputes that digest from the WORKING TREE and fails when it disagrees with the recorded one, naming both values and the fix. `--write` regenerates the stamp. This is a tree-level guarantee only: it never reads individual commits, so a branch that splits the template/ edit from the stamp regeneration into two commits still passes at the tip.

Per-commit enforcement -- every commit touching template/ also touches crates/houserules/payload.stamp, not only the branch tip -- is `houserules check-commit`'s job: this entry's own `check` (type co-change, if template/**, then crates/houserules/payload.stamp) declares `per_commit: true`, the opt-in that runs a co-change check per commit there, over the PR's full range in CI (the opt-in exists because a range-level co-change entry -- process.evals-rerun's, say -- books a different, range-only economy on purpose; check-commit never applies per-commit semantics to one without the flag). check-commit also exempts a commit whose PARENT tree predates payload.stamp's own introduction, so this retroactively-applied check never flags history from before the mechanism existed. After changing anything under template/: run `cargo run --quiet --bin payload-stamp-gate -- --write` and commit the regenerated payload.stamp in the SAME commit as the template/ change -- check-commit rejects a split, the payload-stamp gate alone would not. Once paired, that commit touches crates/houserules/payload.stamp, a path CommitSplit's own, unmodified prefix match already attributes to crates/houserules -- no release-please plugin surface needed.

The per-commit co-change check proves PRESENCE only: that the commit touches both paths, never that the digest it wrote is the tree's true one. Only the tree-level gate above -- payload-stamp-gate run with no arguments, which mise run lint runs in CI on every PR -- recomputes the digest and proves CORRECTNESS, so an intermediate commit can carry a stale digest and still pass check-commit; the tree-level gate at the branch tip is what actually blocks a wrong stamp from reaching main. Observed live at batch 27 T4 (HR-136): the commit that first added AGENTS.md to SEED_ONCE shipped a payload.stamp digest that did not match the tracked template/ tree, check-commit still reported `ok` for it, and only the next `mise run lint` run (payload-stamp-gate over the working tree) caught the mismatch; fixed forward in the very next commit, never by amending the wrong one.

source.ref: batch 24 task-1 fix round 4, the owner's 5.71 rejection (design.md 5.72); fix round 5 added the per-commit check-commit enforcement; fix round 6 scoped it to per_commit: true and added the retroactivity guard; batch 27 T4 fix round 1 added the presence-vs-correctness distinction after that task's own SEED_ONCE commit shipped a wrong digest that check-commit passed

entries.summary: A Release-As footer must survive aggregation: keep its empty commit or restate it on a crates-touching commit; no other body line starts 'Release-As:'.
body: Verify after any history rewrite with git log --grep '^Release-As:' - exactly one hit, the intended one. Release-please reads the footer from any commit in the release window; a competing line at a body line start creates a second footer.

entries.summary: release-please is the only tool that creates a GitHub Release here; dist uploads into it (create-release = false) and never calls gh release create.
body: T2 live (2026-09-13): both tools created v0.3.0 -- release-please on the tag push, then dist's host job failed at gh release create ('a release with the same tag name already exists'; design.md 5.77, HR-118). crates/houserules/tests/dist_workspace_config.rs pins both halves.

When wiring any new release-adjacent automation, enumerate the external resources each tool WRITES (releases, tags, PRs, comments), not only the commits it authors, and name exactly one creator per resource.

source.ref: batch 24 close branch review; T2 create-collision (design.md 5.77)

entries.summary: Prove adopter-facing changes with a throwaway seeded repo: init from the released kit, open a PR, and require the seeded knowledge workflow green end to end.
body: One green PR run proves the installer alias, the binary, and the gates together. Steps (batch 24 close, HR-063): create a private throwaway repository; run houserules init from the RELEASED kit (a downloaded archive, not the dev build); push and open a PR; the seeded knowledge workflow must curl the latest-alias installer inside the runner and pass check-knowledge, check-backlog, and audit. Capture the run JSON and full log into the batch workspace.

The CLI token usually lacks delete_repo: book the owner's deletion of the throwaway repo in the same turn the proof lands. Never use the tag-pilot checkout for this (houserules.tag-pilot-is-read-only).

entries.summary: mise's minimum_release_age (default 24h) keeps a repository's first-ever release from resolving via @latest for a day; later releases fall back unaffected.
body: Verified live at v0.3.0 (batch 24 T3b): the plain documented command failed with 'no versions found ... matching date filter' until the release aged 24h; MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=0s proved the channel itself correct. filter_by_date filters the release list before @latest takes the newest survivor (mise src/toolset/tool_version.rs, read live 2026-09-13).
On release day, verify the mise channel with the override and record both runs; the documented command needs no change.

source.ref: batch 24 T3b report, part B capture set

entries.summary: While the branch changes generated output, run controller gates and update/render through the tree binary, never the installed houserules.
body: The tree binary: `cargo run --release --quiet --bin houserules --`.

The installed `houserules` on PATH is last release's build: it cannot see a change this branch has not shipped yet, and can reject a valid command outright on a schema or engine change the tree already carries.
Reinstall the released build after merge: `cargo install --path crates/houserules --bin houserules`.

This instruction is repository-specific: only a repository that builds `houserules` from source (this one, and any fork) has a tree to build from at all; an adopter's installed binary is already the released build, with no such tree beside it.

entries.summary: Past 1.0, a CLI command/flag change or a schema constraint change is a breaking change: get an owner ruling and bump the major version.
body: The frozen CLI surface: the 20 `Command` variants `crates/houserules/src/main.rs` defines, enumerated by the `no_subcommand_carries_a_long_about_beyond_its_short_one` test (`cargo test --bin houserules no_subcommand_carries_a_long_about_beyond_its_short_one`, asserts the count) and captured verbatim by `cargo run --release --quiet --bin houserules -- --help`.

The frozen schema surface: `knowledge/schema.json`, `template/knowledge/schema.json`, `backlog/schema.json`, `template/backlog/schema.json`, `.claude/schemas/deliverables.json`, and `template/.claude/schemas/deliverables.json` -- their constraints, not a prose restatement of them. `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` pins each copy to its blob id at the freeze; design.md 5.82 carries the six ids.

Adding, removing, or renaming a subcommand or flag, or tightening or loosening a required field, an enum, a textList floor, or an id-shape pattern in any of the six schema files needs an owner ruling and a major-version bump, never a patch or minor release.
Neither surface is gated mechanically by this entry; design.md 5.82 is the durable record an owner supersession amends (process.owner-rulings-need-owner-supersession).

entries.summary: The main ruleset rejects pushes whose commits lack the 8 required checks: even a one-line tick rides a branch and PR; only a green PR head ff-merges clean.
body: Observed live 2026-09-15 (the HR-081 close): a direct one-commit push to main failed GH013 'Changes must be made through a pull request' / '8 of 8 required status checks are expected', while the ff-only merge push of batch-26's green PR head minutes earlier landed (its commits carried the PR's passing checks; only the approving-review rule reported as bypassed).

Consequence for the runbook's restamp step and finishing-a-feature step 8: a post-merge restamp or tick commit goes on a short branch with its own PR and check run, then merges ff-only - never a direct push.
The owner's GitHub UI merge of a release PR is unaffected; the rule binds CLI pushes of unchecked commits.

entries.summary: A dependency with a C build script (a `-sys` crate) breaks the windows-gnu cross check unless ci.yml installs a mingw-w64 C compiler first.
body: Every dependency before axoupdater (HR-133, batch 27 T2) was pure Rust, so `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --all-targets --locked` (houserules.platform-gated-tests' cheap proxy) never invoked a C compiler and passed on a bare ubuntu-latest runner.

axoupdater's github_releases/blocking features pull in aws-lc-sys (rustls' crypto provider via reqwest): its `cc`-crate build script compiles plain C sources (jitterentropy, s2n-bignum's wrapper, BoringSSL C files) on every target it builds for, windows-gnu included, and needs a real `x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc` on PATH to cross-compile those from ubuntu. GitHub's ubuntu-latest runner-images manifest carries no mingw-w64 package by default (checked against actions/runner-images' Ubuntu 24.04 README, 2026-09-15). Without it the build fails `error occurred in cc-rs: failed to find tool "x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc": No such file or directory (os error 2)` (captured against this exact aws-lc-sys 0.45.0 before any mingw toolchain was on PATH).

A separate, unrelated fact about the same crate: its windows x86_64 assembly ships as pre-generated NASM (`.asm`) objects one directory (`win-x86_64`), shared byte-for-byte by the MSVC and GNU ABIs; building them from source needs a real `nasm` executable unless the opt-in `prebuilt-nasm` feature (or `AWS_LC_SYS_PREBUILT_NASM`) is set, in which case the crate copies its own bundled `.obj` files instead. This tree already carries `prebuilt-nasm` -- not from aws-lc-sys's own default (`all-bindings`), but because rustls's and rustls-webpki's own `aws-lc-rs` feature each forward `aws-lc-rs/prebuilt-nasm` once the aws-lc-rs crypto provider is selected (confirmed with `cargo tree -e features -p aws-lc-sys`, and by rustc receiving `--cfg 'feature="prebuilt-nasm"'` in a verbose `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` build) -- so no leg anywhere in this repository ever needs a real `nasm` install; the mingw-w64 package above is for the plain C sources only.

Every other target already has (or dist itself provisions) a working C compiler without any ci.yml change: macOS runners ship Xcode's command-line tools, GitHub's windows runners ship MSVC, and `dist plan --output-format=json`'s own `artifacts_matrix` runs the two musl release legs un-containerized on ubuntu-22.04(-arm) with `packages_install: apt-get install musl-tools` -- dist's own provisioning, never ci.yml's. Only houserules' own additional windows-gnu cross-check proxy (a job no other target needs, since it exists solely as a cheap Linux-hosted stand-in for a real Windows build) needed the new step.

Fix landed alongside axoupdater: ci.yml's `checks` job installs `gcc-mingw-w64-x86-64` via apt-get right before `mise run lint`. Verified locally with a portable llvm-mingw toolchain (mstorsjo/llvm-mingw's prebuilt tarball) on PATH, since this sandbox had neither root nor a system package manager to install the Ubuntu package directly; the two toolchains provide the same `x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc`/`-ar` binary names cc-rs looks for, so the substitution is representative of the C-compiler requirement, though only a real CI run with the actual apt package proves the wiring end to end (HR-137 tracks that confirmation, along with the `rust` job's macos-latest/windows-latest legs and the release build's five targets, none of which has actually run since this dependency landed).

Any future `-sys` crate addition re-triggers the C-compiler half of this: check whether it needs a live C compiler for windows-gnu specifically (a Rust-only or fully-prebuilt-for-every-target dependency does not), and add the runner's compiler package in the same commit if it does.

entries.summary: AGENTS.md is the cross-harness instruction surface; CLAUDE.md is a one-line pointer to it; every seeded text stays harness-neutral.
body: Batch 27 T4 (HR-136): `template/AGENTS.md` carries the canonical project instructions -- the substance CLAUDE.md alone used to carry, rephrased for 'your agent'/'the agent' rather than 'Claude'. `template/CLAUDE.md` is exactly `@AGENTS.md`, the one-line import Claude Code's own docs endorse (code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md, verified 2026-09-15). Both join `SEED_ONCE`: `init` writes each once, `update` never overwrites an existing copy of either, and backfills whichever one a later kit release adds to an install an older release already seeded.

Every seeded text -- the three template skills, template knowledge entries, template docs -- names 'your agent'/'the agent', never 'Claude', as the addressee (writing-style.instructions-cover-the-state-space: an instruction that assumes Claude Code's skills auto-load or its subagents exist stops holding for every other harness). `.claude/rules/*`, `.claude/agents/*`, and the SessionStart hook (`tools/claude-session-start.sh`) stay genuinely Claude-Code-specific mechanisms; AGENTS.md's own 'Working with other harnesses' section names them as optional accelerations a harness with none of the three still fully covers by reading AGENTS.md and running the `houserules` commands it names.

This repository adopts its own design: root `AGENTS.md` carries this repository's own instructions, not the generic template's (its batch lifecycle names a user gate and this repository's own `process.sequential-agents` ruling), and root `CLAUDE.md` is the same one-line pointer -- both edited directly, since neither is `KIT_OWNED`: `houserules.template-is-the-source`'s byte-identity pin (`crates/houserules/tests/dogfood.rs`) never covers a `SEED_ONCE` path.

The kit's own gate carries the same design, not only the seeded texts: `check_base` (crates/houserules/src/rules/check.rs) requires AGENTS.md to exist and spends the 200-line/12288-byte instruction budget on it; it tolerates an absent CLAUDE.md entirely (no finding), budgeting it only when present, at the same limits. No `knowledge/areas.json` area glob may name `CLAUDE.md`: an adopter who deletes the now-optional pointer would leave that glob matching nothing, and the dead-glob gate fails the whole base for it -- this is why the docs area's own glob list carries `AGENTS.md` but never `CLAUDE.md`, in this repository's own `knowledge/areas.json` and in `template/knowledge/areas.json` alike. Batch 27 T4 fix round 1 shipped the design in code before this clause existed to say so; fix round 2 added this clause after the gap between code and entry was itself filed as a finding.
